_note: Three ANSWER FORMS for the 11 public sample cases, hand-written for the
answer-form experiment in scripts/answer_form_eval.py. Nothing here is
shipped; this file exists only to be scored.
THE RULE THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT ABOUT FORM. Where the shipped answer
is WRONG -- case124 (Bipolar Forceps, gold Cadiere Forceps), case126 (No,
gold Yes), case132 (Yes, gold No) -- every form repeats the same wrong
content. A form that quietly corrected them would be measuring
correctness, not shape.
HOW THE SENTENCES WERE WRITTEN, stated because it biases the result. Each
is a STEM INVERSION of the organizers' question: 'What organ is being
manipulated?' -> 'The organ being manipulated is the uterine horn.' That
is the natural declarative answer, and it is also the construction the
organizers' own sentence references use, so these are the most FAVOURABLE
sentence forms available rather than strawmen. Read the sentence-form
numbers as an upper bound.
No string here is byte-identical to any gold reference; a test pins that,
so no form can win by copying the answer key. It caught one on the first
run: case127's stem inversion, 'The organ being manipulated is the uterine
horn.', IS gold reference[1] verbatim, and would have scored a free 1.0000
under every condition. It was replaced with 'The surgeon is manipulating
the uterine horn.' -- which is itself the finding worth keeping: the
organizers' sentence references ARE stem inversions of their questions, so
a sentence-form answer built the natural way lands very close to them.
